meta.title: Why does a child trust strangers online? | Power of Words
meta.description: Teach your child to recognize manipulation and protect themselves from toxic influence online. A game-based format for kids aged 8–12.

hero.headline: Your child has “friends” you don’t know!
hero.subheadline: Every day they communicate with people who shape their thoughts and decisions. It’s time to teach them to tell real friends from fake ones.

media.alt: Child staring at phone screen alone while parent sits nearby unaware

pain.title: Manipulation starts long before the teenage years
pain.body:
Your child sees hundreds of messages, videos, and posts every day — and has no tools to distinguish truth from lies.

Online “friends”, gaming chats, ads — all of them have learned to speak to children in their language. Critical thinking has not.

Children who cannot recognize manipulation grow up more vulnerable: they easily give in to peer pressure, fall into toxic relationships, and struggle to say “no”.

solution.title: “Power of Words” — a detective drama that teaches thinking
solution.body: 50 episodes, 13 critical thinking lessons. The child plays — but actually learns to protect themselves.
bullets: 🔍 Recognizes manipulation in texts, videos, and conversations
🧠 Learns to ask questions instead of just believing
🤝 Understands who is a real friend and who is not
🛡️ Learns to say “no” without fear or guilt

social_proof.quote: For the first time in years, my son started asking himself: “Mom, why are they saying that?” — it changed everything.
social_proof.author: Oksana, mother of 10-year-old Maksym

faq.q: Is it a game or a learning course?
faq.a: Both at the same time. “Power of Words” looks like a detective series, but each episode contains a hidden lesson in critical thinking.

faq.q: What age is it suitable for?
faq.a: Ideally 8–12 years old. At this age, children are most receptive to new thinking patterns and have not yet formed strong biases.

faq.q: How much time is needed daily?
faq.a: 15–20 minutes per episode. Flexible schedule — the child can return at any convenient time.

faq.q: Is registration required for the demo?
faq.a: No. The demo episode is fully open — no registration, no subscription, no data entry.
